title: Change Job New User Experience Initiation Improvements
desc: We streamline the initiation of Change Job templates that have the simplified user experience enabled.
benefits: This feature improves the user experience when a user initiates a Change Job.
changes:
Prior to this feature, when you initiated a consolidated Change Job template with subprocesses and the simplified user interface enabled, Workday would: 
     • Display an intermediary initiation page with a Submit button. 
    • Create an in-progress Change Job event that displayed in the worker’s history after you clicked Submit. 
    • Display a main Change Job business process workflow page with the subprocesses. 
    • Update the in-progress Change Job event after the user clicked Submit again. 
    • For a Request Transfer initiated through Recruiting: Display the Revise Job Change event in the user’s inbox that they can edit directly. 
 Now when a user initiates a Change Job, we simplify the workflow by: 
     • Displaying the main Change Job business process workflow page. 
    • Dynamically displaying relevant subprocesses after users click the Next button. 
    • Waiting to create an in-progress Change Job event until after the user completes the subprocesses and clicks Submit. 
    • For a Request Transfer initiated through Recruiting: Display the Revise Job Change event in the user’s inbox as view-only with a Make Changes button. 
 This feature reduces unnecessary or accidental in-progress Change Job events. 
 Move to New Manager 
 We update the experience when you select a worker who isn’t a manager in the Who will be this person’s manager after the move? field. Prior to this feature, Workday displayed an alert and redirected you to the Move to New Manager task. Now, Workday displays a warning message and a Move to New Manager button that you can select to proceed. This feature isn’t available in mobile.

title: Additional Payroll Data Enhancements
desc: With this release, we improve the Additional Payroll Data experience by enabling you to view and download attachments that third-party payroll vendors provide directly on the Additional Payroll Data task. We also streamline how you interact with the task by enabling you to collapse field groups.
benefits: Access to vendor-provided attachments streamlines onboarding by letting you download, complete, and re-upload templates directly within the Additional Payroll Data task, reducing manual data-entry errors. Collapsible field groups enable you to keep the task focused on the fields that need your attention.
changes:
Vendor Attachments 
 We update the Additional Payroll Data task so you can now view and download attachments provided by third-party payroll vendors, such as a template document that you can fill in and re-upload into the Additional Payroll Data form. 
 
 Field Group Display 
 Additionally, field groups are now in collapsible sections on the Additional Payroll Data task.

title: Mass Job Change
desc:
With this release, you can process high-volume staffing updates using Mass Job Change on Mass Action Tables. 
 You opt in to Mass Job Change to transition from Mass Actions Worksheets to Mass Job Change Tables including mass Change Organization Assignments and simple Mass Compensation Changes. 
 For U.S. Federal customers, you can view and process personnel action requests on the Personnel Action Requests tab.
benefits:
• Faster Execution Speed: Reduces operational processing time compared with manual data entry, legacy worksheets, or complex EIB file uploads. 
    • High-Volume Processing at Scale: Manage and execute up to 5,000 job changes in a single interface. 
    • Enhanced Data Accuracy and Risk Reduction: Real-time validations and dynamic delta views highlight field changes before you submit, helping reduce downstream data errors. 
    • Greater Agility with Out-of-Sequence Support: Insert job changes for multiple workers even when a worker already has subsequent staffing events scheduled, without manually restructuring events. 
    • Scalable Governance and Auditing: Support data sign-offs with integrated mass approvals, comments, and rescinds for compliance and auditability. 
    • Empowered HR Operations and HRBPs: Gives HR Business Partners a table-based interface for mass job changes, reducing reliance on central HR Operations and specialized file processing. 
    • Flexible Target Population Selection: Select populations using multiple methods—including pasting up to 5,000 worker or position IDs or selecting multiple supervisory organizations (with subordinates)—with worker preview before you generate a table.
changes:
With this release, Mass Job Change delivers new capabilities for high-volume Change Job processing. 
 Mass Job Change Tables 
 You can now initiate and process change jobs en masse using Mass Job Change Tables. You can generate an interactive table for up to 5,000 workers. Workday performs real-time validation and displays errors in the table as you edit. 
 You can view and modify rows only if you have appropriate security group access. Mass Job Change respects role-based and intersectional security, such as location, supervisory organization, or cost center. 
 Tables include tabs for Change Job, Organization Assignments, and Compensation Change. There is also a Personnel Action Requests tab for U.S. Federal customers. Fixed columns such as Worker, Worker ID, and Status remain visible across tabs. 
 For consistency, we rename mass action tasks, reports, and initiating actions from Launch to Start: 
     • The Launch Mass Action Event task is now the Start Mass Action task. 
    • The Launch Mass Change Job report is now the Start Mass Job Change report. 
    • Initiating action names on the Mass Action Event business process policy are now Start Mass Action. 
 Mass Job Change Experience 
 You can now opt in to transition from Mass Actions Worksheets. 
 In 2026R2, this opt-in is available for 6 months. After you opt in, you can't switch back to Mass Action Worksheets for mass Change Job processing. 
 Starting in 2027R1, Mass Job Change automatically replaces Mass Actions Worksheets for mass Change Job for all customers. 
 Initiate 
 You can initiate a mass job change by accessing the Start Mass Action task or the Start Mass Job Change report. 
 When you use the Start Mass Action task, you can select your target population by: 
     • Reports 
    • List of Position IDs or Worker IDs 
    • Supervisory Organizations 
 You can also use the Start Mass Job Change report to select your population. Optional: You can copy and customize this Workday-delivered report to modify filter facets. 
 Once the population is selected, Workday generates the table and validates positions. The Positions Excluded from Mass Action grid lists the workers excluded when Workday generates the table. 
 Complete 
 You can sort and filter rows, mass edit, and single-row edit. Workday runs validation after each mass edit and single-row edit. 
 You can remove rows that you don't want to process so that only the intended workers remain. 
 Tables display a row status summary with counts for Valid, Invalid, Not Edited, Warning and Removed Transaction rows that you can access. 
 You can track transaction statuses and see added, modified, and removed values at the cell level. You can interact with a modified cell to view current and proposed values. 
 The Change Job and Organization Assignments tabs show added, modified, and removed values for delta view supported fields . These aren't available on the Compensation Change tab. 
 Removed Transactions shows the count of manually removed rows and rows not processed on completion. Reviewers and approvers only see rows they're authorized to access. 
 When edits are complete, click Submit Table. On submit, Workday processes the full table: all rows regardless of status. Note: Partial table submissions aren't supported. After you submit the table, submit the My Tasks item to progress or complete the workflow. 
 Review and approve 
 You can now route mass job change events through review and approval in Workday. On Review Mass Job Change, reviewers receive an editable My Tasks item. On Approve Mass Job Change, approvers receive a read-only My Tasks item. Edit and Mass Edit aren't available on the approve step. 
 Send back, deny, and rescind 
 Submit replaces Mark as Complete on complete, review, and approve My Tasks items. 
 Send Back and Deny are available on review and approve items only, not on Complete Mass Action. 
 You can select Rescind from the related actions menu of archived Mass Action Event items on the Archive tab of My Tasks to undo a completed event. You receive a notification when rescind processing completes. 
 Out of order 
 When out of order is enabled for Change Job, tables include workers with future blocking staffing events for the selected effective date. Workday displays out of order warnings in the table when edits create an out of order event. 
 Mass comments 
 You can add comments to rows on the Change Job tab using Mass Edit. Comments stay on each worker's Change Job event record when the Change Job event is processed after submission of the table in the last step of the mass action workflow. 
 Mass Propose Compensation Change 
 You can process compensation changes as part of a mass Change Job business process. When you initiate a mass Change Job process and Propose Compensation Change is configured as a sub-process, you can access the Compensation Change tab of the mass action interface to view and edit compensation changes. 
 To use this feature, you must have Compensation Change templates that are enabled for the Change Job business process type. Columns on the Compensation Change tab follow the fields configured on your Compensation Change template. 
 Field and option visibility in the Compensation Change tab and Mass Edit modal depends on the user’s permissions for the domains associated with those fields. Users can only view and modify compensation data for workers they are authorized to manage. 
 If your Compensation Change template includes the Guidelines section, you can bulk-assign: 
     • Compensation Package. 
    • Grade. 
    • Grade Profile. 
    • Progression Start Date. 
    • Step. 
 If your Compensation Change template includes both the Hourly and Salary sections, you can increase or decrease existing salary and hourly plan amounts or percentages. Note that this process modifies plans already assigned to a worker and does not assign new plans. 
 When you run the mass Change Job process with Propose Compensation Change as a sub-process, Workday creates a corresponding compensation event for each worker, so compensation rules and defaulting run based on the proposed job changes. 
 This feature isn’t applicable to all workers. It excludes: 
     • Contingent workers. 
    • Workers whose primary compensation basis is Manage Basis Total (MBT). If a change made during the mass Change Job process causes a worker to become MBT-eligible, Workday won’t update their compensation. 
 You can view current and proposed compensation changes in the Compensation Group Event Details report.

title: Language Support for Talent Highlights
desc:
With this release, we extend language support for Talent Highlights. 
We now support all languages available in Workday for: 
     • The source data that we include when generating Talent Highlights content. 
    • The AI-generated Talent Highlights output that we provide to managers.
benefits: We remove barriers to adopting Talent Highlights for organizations that use languages other than English, and we make Talent functionality more consistent across different languages.
changes:
Supported Languages 
We now support Talent Highlights in all languages supported in Workday, except: 
     • Chinese (Hong Kong) 
    • Chinese (Simplified) 
    • Chinese (Traditional) 
    • Japanese 
    • Thai 
 
 Talent Highlights Interface and Output Text 
 When a manager uses a supported language, we now surface this information in the same language as the manager’s system: 
     • Talent Highlights content that the manager generates. 
    • Details about the source data, which managers can view in the Data Sources section. 
    • Interface text for generating, viewing, editing, and deleting Talent Highlights. 
 If the manager has a preferred display language, we use this language. Otherwise, we use their preferred locale, their location, or the default tenant language. For details, see the Concept: Country-Specific Information, Locales, and Languages link in the Related Information section. 
 If an error occurs while the manager is generating Talent Highlights content, we surface the error message in English only. 
 
 Language Support for Source Data 
We support source data for Talent Highlights in any of the supported languages.

title: Override Change Job Field Access Using Security Groups
desc: Workday enables you to configure security groups for specific Change Job template fields.
benefits: This provides you with further flexibility when configuring which users can access which Change Job template fields.
changes:
Maintain Functionality for Staffing Transactions Task 
 We enable you to configure security groups for specific Change Job template fields. You can configure them on the new Change Job Template Field Security tab on the Maintain Functionality for Staffing Transactions task for the Change Job business process type. Your configuration applies when the field is included on a template. Your configuration here will override your configuration on the Configure Optional Fields task, unless the field is Hide for All or Not Enterable for All. 
 This feature doesn’t apply to these fields: 
     • Effective Date 
    • Reason 
    • Location 
    • Which team will this person be moving to? 
    • Manager and Team after Change 
    • Who will be this person's manager after the move? 
    • Change Organization Assignment fields (Business Unit, Company, Cost Center, Custom Organizations, Fund, Gift, Grant, Program, Region). 
 SOAP Web Service Operations 
 Workday delivers these new web service operations (secured to the Set Up: Staffing domain in the Staffing functional area) in v47.0 to enable you to load and retrieve data from the Change Job Template Field Security tab on the Maintain Functionality for Staffing Transactions task: 
     • Put Change Job Template Field Security Configuration 
    • Get Change Job Template Field Security Configurations 
 See the SOAP API Change Log link under Related Information. 
 
One-Time Conversion 
 If your tenant doesn’t have an active template with the Change Job initiating action, we run a one-time conversion to copy your existing configuration of security groups if they aren’t included on the Change Job business process security policy and are configured on these domains: 
     • Staffing Actions: Academic Pay 
    • Staffing Actions: Administrator 
    • Staffing Actions: Additional Job Classifications 
    • Staffing Actions: Contract Details 
    • Staffing Actions: Business Title 
    • Staffing Actions: Change Job Date and Reason 
    • Staffing Actions: Job Profile 
    • Staffing Actions: Location 
    • Staffing Actions: Select or Create Position 
    • Staffing Actions: Move Manager's Team 
 We recommend that you review the results of the conversion on the new Change Job Template Field Security tab on the Maintain Functionality for Staffing Transactions task for the Change Job business process type. 
 Staffing Actions: Select or Create Position 
 The conversion doesn’t run for the Staffing Actions: Select or Create Position domain if your tenant has an active template with the Change Job initiating action. However, this means that if you have configured security groups on the domain that aren’t included on the Change Job business process security policy, those groups won’t have access to the Position, Create Position, and Job Requisition fields. 
 Workday recommends that you review the configuration on the Staffing Actions: Select or Create Position domain. Add the necessary security groups to those fields on the new Change Job Template Field Security tab on the Maintain Functionality for Staffing Transactions task for the Change Job business process type.

title: Advanced Lookup Table Snapshot Selection
desc: Workday enhances the View/Edit Lookup Table interface by introducing a prompt to select a specific snapshot when working with advanced lookup tables. This enables payroll administrators to view or modify data for a single snapshot, though they retain the option to load all snapshots simultaneously if needed.
benefits: This update addresses performance issues associated with large lookup tables by reducing the amount of data processed during a single session. By selecting a specific snapshot, administrators might experience faster page loads and improved system stability when maintaining high-volume payroll data.
changes:
We introduce a new Advanced Lookup Table Snapshot prompt that appears on the View/Edit Lookup Table task when you select an advanced lookup table that contains one or more snapshots. The new prompt does not appear if you select a standard lookup table or an advanced lookup table without existing snapshots. 
 When you select a snapshot and click Ok, Workday displays only the data for that specific snapshot. If you don't select a snapshot, Workday displays all data for the table that you select.

title: Enhanced Change Job Experience Conversion
desc:
We are retiring the old Change Job Experience and moving to the New Enhanced Change Job Experience for 26R2. To help complete the move, we deliver a conversion to support the deprecation of the legacy Change Job experience. 
 The conversion will: 
     • Migrate legacy Start Job Change user interface templates to the new enhanced user interface. 
    • Generate new templates if they don't exist in your tenant for these initiating actions: Change Job, Request Transfer, Change Location, Change Contingent Worker Details. 
    • Perform a security conversion if you don't have an active template configured for the Change Job initiating action. That security conversion will map domain security groups to Configure Optional Fields and unconstrained role-based security groups to Maintain Functionality for Staffing Transactions. 
    • Not perform the security conversion if you have an active template configured for the Change Job initiating action.
benefits: This conversion automatically migrates any customers who have not yet adopted the enhanced Change Job experience.
changes:
Workday migrates your current Change Job configuration to support the enhanced Change Job experience. This means that Workday will display a Change Job Template with the enhanced user experience when you initiate a Change Job using a task or initiating action. The changes Workday makes to your tenant depends on what you’ve currently configured. 
 In progress Change Job events are also migrated to the enhanced Change Job experience. 
 Existing Change Job Templates 
 Workday updates existing Change Job templates for any templates that include the Start Job Change initiating action to use the enhanced Change Job user experience. 
Workday hides the Enable Enhanced UI for this Template check box on the Maintain Change Job Templates task. 
 Any templates that you create after this conversion will automatically use the enhanced Change Job experience. You won’t be able to create templates using the legacy Change Job experience. 
 New Change Job Templates 
 Workday creates a separate Change Job template for each of the following Change Job business process initiating actions if your tenant doesn’t already have a template for that initiating action: 
     • Change Job regardless of whether the action is configured on the corresponding business process policy in your tenant. 
    • Request Transfer regardless of whether the action is configured on the corresponding business process policy in your tenant. 
    • Change Location only if the action is currently configured on the corresponding business process policy in your tenant. 
    • Change Contingent Worker only if the action is currently configured on the corresponding business process policy in your tenant. 
 Workday will create templates for those initiating actions with the following configuration: 
     • Enable Enhanced UI for this Template check box: Selected, and hidden on the template. 
    • Apply this Template to Review and Approve Steps check box: Selected. 
    • Select Reason for Template prompt: Active reasons configured on your tenant on the Maintain Event Categories and Reasons task added to this prompt. 
    • Make this Template Inactive check box: View only. 
 You can’t inactivate or delete: 
     • The newly created templates. 
    • Any existing active templates you already configured for those initiating actions. However, you can delete existing inactivated templates for those initiating actions. 
 Workday dynamically includes relevant sections and fields based on the specific initiating actions and staffing security domains currently enabled in your tenant: 
     • Change Job and Request Transfer:     • Includes sections and fields for the relevant staffing actions domains that are enabled on your tenant. They also include all sub-processes that are included in these configurations on the business process: Configure Consolidated Template, Configure Rule-Based Consolidated Template, and Configure Consolidated Template Override. 
    • When a user initiates Change Job as a subprocess from other staffing transactions (such as Recruiting or Manage Probation), Workday uses the Change Job template if there’s no organization change, and the Request Transfer template if there’s an organization change. 
 
    • Change Location:     • Includes the Work Location, Additional Job Classifications, and Administrative sections if the corresponding staffing actions domains are enabled on your tenant. 
    • If your tenant has Configure Consolidated Template, Configure Rule-Based Consolidated Template, or Configure Consolidated Template Override configured with these sub-processes, Workday will configure the template to include them: Propose Compensation, Assign Collective Agreement. 
 
    • Change Contingent Worker:     • Includes the Contract Details section if the corresponding staffing actions domain is enabled on your tenant. 
    • If your tenant has Configure Consolidated Template, Configure Rule-Based Consolidated Template, or Configure Consolidated Template Override configured with the Assign Collective Agreement sub-process, Workday will include it in the template. 
 
 Security Configuration Conversion to Configure Optional Fields 
 This security configuration conversion for the Configure Optional Fields task runs if your tenant doesn’t have an active template with the Change Job initiating action. 
 Note: Workday won't perform this security conversion if you have an active template configured for the Change Job initiating action. 
 The legacy Change Job experience secured fields to various staffing domains. The enhanced Change Job experience secures fields to only the Staffing Actions: Change Job Date and Reason domain. The Change Organization Assignments subprocess within the Change Job business process is secured to the Staffing Organizations: Header domain. Users with View and Modify access to those domains can edit all fields on the Job Change and Change Organization Assignment sections in a Change Job event. You can configure field visibility and access on the Configure Optional Fields task. 
 This conversion looks at your existing configurations on these staffing domains, and applies that configuration to the applicable fields in either the Change Job or Change Organization Assignments functional areas on the Configure Optional Fields task: 
     • Staffing Actions. The conversion uses your configuration on this super domain if the relevant subdomains are inheriting access from it. 
    • Staffing Actions: Academic Pay 
    • Staffing Actions: Administrator 
    • Staffing Actions: Additional Job Classifications 
    • Staffing Actions: Contract Details 
    • Staffing Actions: Business Title 
    • Staffing Actions: Change Job Date and Reason 
    • Staffing Actions: Job Profile 
    • Staffing Actions: Location 
    • Staffing Actions: Select or Create Position 
    • Staffing Actions: Move Manager's Team 
    • Staffing Organizations: Business Unit 
    • Staffing Organizations: Company 
    • Staffing Organizations: Cost Center 
    • Staffing Organizations: Custom Organization 
    • Staffing Organizations: Grant, Fund, Program, Gift 
    • Staffing Organizations: Header 
    • Staffing Organizations: Region 
 The security configuration conversion for the Configure Optional Fields task: 
     • Doesn’t run if your tenant has an active template with the Change Job initiating action. In that case, Workday recommends that you review your security configuration and update your field configuration on the Change Job or Change Organization Assignments functional areas on the Configure Optional Fields task. Example: You have suspended the Staffing Actions: Business Title domain because you wanted to hide the Business Title field from users. Your tenant has an active template with the Change Job initiating action. After the conversion, users can now view the Business Title field. You configure it on the Configure Optional Fields task to hide it. 
    • Doesn’t take into account any security groups you’ve added to the Change Job business process security policy that you haven’t activated using the Activate Pending Security Policy Changes task. 
    • Doesn’t remove your existing configurations on the Configure Optional Fields task. If you have previously used Configure Optional Fields to set certain fields on Change Job and Change Organization Assignments as hidden or not enterable, those settings will remain in place. The conversion will only add any new fields or security groups necessary for the conversion. 
 You can use the View Configure Optional Fields for Change Job Before and After Conversion report (secured to the Set Up: Staffing domain) to review the results of the conversion. 
 View Only Field Configuration 
 When a Security Group is configured on any action on the Change Job Business Process Security Policy, and that group has only View access rights to a relevant staffing domain, Workday runs the following conversion: 
     • Automatically generates new entries or updates existing entries for the specific fields secured by that staffing domain within the Configure Optional Fields task for Change Job. 
    • Adds the relevant Security Group to these field entries with the access level set to Not Enterable For. 
    • Selects the Evaluate All Security Groups check box. 
 Example: If the Manager security group has View Only access to the Staffing Actions: Job Profile domain, the conversion creates an entry in the Configure Optional Fields task, and makes the Manager security group Not Enterable For these fields: 
     • Job Profile 
    • Job Title 
 Hidden Field Configuration 
 If a security group does not have View or Modify permissions to a relevant staffing domain, Workday: 
     • Automatically generates new entries or updates existing entries for the specific fields secured by that staffing domain within the Configure Optional Fields task for Change Job. 
    • Adds the relevant Security Group to these field entries with the access level set to hidden. 
    • Selects the Evaluate All Security Groups check box. 
 Required Field Configuration 
 The legacy Change Job experience didn’t allow you to set fields as required. Therefore, the conversion doesn’t generate any new entries on the Configure Optional Fields task to make fields required. The conversion will update existing entries for the specific fields secured by the relevant staffing domain on the Configure Optional Fields task for Change Job. 
 If a field is currently set as Required for All in Configure Optional Fields, and the relevant staffing domain grants a specific security group Modify access to that field, the conversion will adjust the requirement and Workday will: 
     • Remove the Required for All setting. 
    • Add the Security Group with Modify access to the Required for setting instead. 
 If a field is currently set as Required for All in Configure Optional Fields, and the relevant staffing domain grants a specific Security Group View Only access to that field, the conversion will adjust the requirement and Workday will: 
     • Remove the Required for All setting. 
    • Add the Security Group to the field's settings as Not Enterable For. 
 Mapping between Staffing Actions Domains and Fields on Change Job Templates 
 The attached StaffingActionsDomainsandChangeJobTemplateFieldMapping.pdf file explains what domains secured which fields on the legacy Change Job experience. You can use it to understand the security configuration conversion for the Configure Optional Fields task. 
 Close the Current Position Field 
 The Close the Current Position field on the Configure Optional Fields task doesn’t apply to the enhanced Change Job experience. After the conversion, your existing configuration on the Close the Current Position field for the Configure Optional Fields task won’t apply. 
 Security Configuration Conversion for Override Field Access 
 This security configuration conversion for role-based unconstrained security groups runs if your tenant doesn’t have an active template with the Change Job initiating action. 
 Note: Workday won't perform this security conversion if you have an active template configured for the Change Job initiating action. 
 This conversion moves role-based unconstrained security groups from these domains to corresponding fields for the Change Job business process on the Maintain Functionality for Staffing Transactions task, if those security groups aren’t configured on the Change Job business process security policy:: 
 Staffing Actions: Academic Pay 
 Staffing Actions: Administrator 
 Staffing Actions: Additional Job Classifications 
 Staffing Actions: Contract Details 
 Staffing Actions: Business Title 
 Staffing Actions: Change Job Date and Reason 
 Staffing Actions: Job Profile 
 Staffing Actions: Location 
 Staffing Actions: Select or Create Position 
 Staffing Actions: Move Manager's Team 
 See the Override Change Job Field Access Using Security Groups release note for more information. 
 Quick Tips 
 Existing Quick Tips that you configured for legacy Change Job don’t display on Change Job templates. After this conversion, they won’t display for users when they access Change Job. You need to reconfigure them using the Guidance Workspace report. Reconfigure them for these templates: 
 Templates that the conversion updated to use the enhanced user interface. 
 New templates created by the conversion. 
 View Change Job Template Field Security Configuration Report 
 We deliver a new View Change Job Template Field Security Configuration report (secured to the Set Up: Staffing domain in the Staffing functional area). You can use this report to view the configuration for a field on these tasks: 
     • Maintain Change Job Templates 
    • Configure Optional Fields 
    • Maintain Functionality for Staffing Transactions

title: Manage Wellness Partner Connections and Use Cases
desc: Workday enables you to manage the connection status and use cases of your wellness partners. From a partner profile, you can add or remove specific use cases, remove a partner’s connection, or approve a reconnection when a previously disconnected partner re-requests access.
benefits: This feature gives you finer control over what data and API use cases a wellness partner can access. You can pause or end partner integrations without backend intervention, so tenant data access stays current and compliant.
changes:
Remove Connection is now available on the wellness partner profile to disconnect a connected partner. 
 Disconnected partners move to the Tenanted Wellness Partners section and display a Disconnected status. 
 Manage Access lets you add or remove specific use cases granted to a connected partner. 
 When a disconnected partner re-requests access, you can approve the request to restore the connection and merge them with their existing tenanted partner instance.

title: Attachments for Payroll Processing Checklists
desc: With this release, Workday adds the ability to upload attachments to items on a payroll processing checklist for Workday Payroll pay groups. You can store supporting files with checklist items during payroll processing and view them from the checklist.
benefits: You can store supporting documentation on payroll processing checklist items in Payroll Hub instead of tracking files outside Workday, which supports audits and handoffs during the pay period.
changes:
Workday enables you to add attachments to payroll processing checklists in Payroll Hub. 
 On a checklist, you can: 
     • Add attachments to payroll processing checklists from the View Payroll Processing Checklist task. 
    • Click Maintain Attachments to upload files to checklist items. 
    • View uploaded files in the Attachments column on the checklist. 
 Attachments only apply to the checklist they were uploaded to and don't carry forward to checklists for future payroll periods. 
 
 When you upload files successfully, Workday displays a confirmation message.

title: Feature Opt-In Removed for Restrict Job Profile Visibility by Country and Organization on Job Requisition Tasks
desc: Workday now enables you to restrict the visibility of job profiles by specific supervisory organizations, companies, countries, or a combination of all three on all job requisition tasks. During these transactions, users will only see job profiles that are valid for that event based on your configured restrictions. This feature applies to the following prompt folders: By Job Family, With Work Study, and With Unions. This feature now doesn’t require you to opt-in before you set it up.
benefits: This feature ensures users are only able to see and choose from job profiles that are appropriate for certain job requisition transactions. It enables you to have distinct job profiles across different portions of your business, which improves the user experience and decreases data discrepancies.
changes:
Workday removes the Restrict Job Profile Visibility by Country and Organization feature on the Maintain Feature Opt-Ins task. This means that Workday now always applies the restrictions you configure on the Restrict to Country and Restrict to Organization fields on the Manage Job Profile business process. 
 Now, during these job requisition tasks, users will only see job profiles that are valid for that event based on your configured restrictions. 
     • Copy Evergreen Requisition 
    • Create Evergreen Requisition 
    • Edit Evergreen Requisition 
    • Start Job Requisition 
    • Copy Evergreen Requisition to Create Job Requisition 
    • Copy Job Requisition 
    • Create Confidential Job Requisition 
    • Create Job Requisition 
    • Create Job Requisition Sub Process 
    • Edit Job Requisition 
 When a user accesses those tasks: 
     • The restricted job profiles won't display in the Job Profile or the Additional Job Profile fields. If the job profile becomes invalid because of a user's supervisory organization, company, or country selections, Workday displays an alert. The user can still submit the event. When testing in Preview Implementation tenants the user will still be able to search for any restricted Job Profile by its name. 
    • They can search for hidden restricted job profiles using the Workday ID if they use the prefix wid:. 
 If you configured at least one country and at least one organization restriction, both values in the staffing transaction need to meet those restrictions in order for the job profile to be available. 
 If you configured multiple values in the Restrict to Country or Restrict to Organization fields, at least one value in that field needs to meet that restriction in order for the job profile to be available. 
 Workday doesn't display the job profile for users if none of these values on the event are in the configured restricted country: 
     • Proposed value in the primary location field. 
    • Proposed value in the additional locations field. 
    • Primary location on the proposed supervisory organization. 
 Workday doesn't display the job profile for users if none of these values on the event contain the organization the job profile is restricted to: 
     • Proposed value in the Company or Supervisory Organization fields. 
    • Default or allowed company on the proposed supervisory organization.

title: Worker Data - Leave Management
desc: Wrokday delivers new leave management options on the Get Workers Data API for partners utilizing the Connected Absence use case. You can now use the Wellness Override and Mapping Setup tasks on the Workday Wellness hub to define eligible worker populations and map critical employment contact and absence plan data.
benefits: This enhancement enables integration between Workday and your wellness partners for absence management. By enabling you to override and map specific leave data, such as employment contacts and accrued time off balances, you ensure that partners receive accurate information without requiring custom integrations.
changes:
User interface changes 
 We make these changes to the user interface: 
 Add a Leave Management section to the Wellness Override task on the Workday Wellness hub. You can configure Leave Management Eligibility and overrides for leave management fields, such as: rule50_75Indicator 
 keyEmployeeIndicator 
 worked hours quantities (perWeekWorkedHoursQuantity, weeklyWorkedHoursQuantity, and daily worked hours quantities) 
 last12MonthPaidHours 
 last8WeeksEarnings 
 accommodatesRestriction 
 
 Add a Leave Management section to the Mapping Setup task on the Workday Wellness hub. You can map: Employment Contacts (up to 3 contact types, such as AdditionalReportingContact, BenefitsCoordinator, ReportingManager, and UnionContact) 
 Sick Absence Plans and Vacation Absence Plans 
 Worker Earnings pay components (for yearToDateEarnings)

title: Proration Based on Work Schedule Calendar
desc:
We now enable pay component proration based on work schedule calendar assignments. You can prorate earnings and deductions using the hours or days defined in each worker's assigned work schedule calendars, with separate calculations for each position when a worker holds multiple positions. We also add a new proration calculation. 
 We introduce a new proration event for Payroll for Australia, Ireland, and the United Kingdom, which triggers proration from midperiod work schedule calendar changes. 
 With this update, we enhance Workday's ability to support workers with multiple positions across Absence, Payroll, and Time Tracking.
benefits: Prorating from work schedule calendars rather than work shift produces calculations that reflect each worker's actual scheduled commitments, which improves accuracy for workers with irregular schedules or multiple positions.
changes:
We add an Enable Proration Using Work Schedule Calendars check box on these tasks (secured to the Set Up: Payroll (Calculations - Payroll Specific) domain in the Core Payroll functional area): 
     • Create Deduction 
    • Create Earning 
 When you select the check box, we also display a new Prorate Using Hours Worked calculation option that you can select when you create or edit pay components. When you enable proration based on work schedule calendars and select this option, Workday references the work schedule calendar assigned to the worker or position instead of the work shift. This ensures that pay accurately reflects the worker's expected schedule for the period, specifically resolving common over- and under-payment issues for midperiod transitions and leaves of absence. 
 If a worker doesn't have a directly assigned work schedule calendar, Workday displays a zero value for the Prorate Using Hours Worked calculation. 
 
 Existing Proration Methods 
 We also update these existing proration methods to reference work schedule calendar assignments when you have enabled work schedule calendars for pay component proration: 
     • Prorate Using Calendar Days 
    • Prorate Using Days Worked 
 For workers without work schedule calendars, Workday uses the worker's work shift when available, or a Monday to Friday work week. 
 When prorating based on days, Workday defines a day as any day with a schedule shift in the work schedule calendar, regardless of duration. When a worker's shift crosses midnight, Workday counts the shift on the day it started. 
 Notes: 
     • When you enable proration based on work schedule calendar, don't select the Prorate Using Annual Working Days proration method. 
    • When you enable proration based on work schedule calendars and use the Prorate Using Calendar Days proration method, the method references only scheduled days. 
 
 Proration Event (AUS, IRL, UK) 
For Payroll for Australia, Ireland, and the United Kingdom, we also deliver the new: 
     • Assign Work Schedule proration event. 
    • Work Schedule Calendar Change proration event category. 
 You can view details of the new proration event and category on the Maintain Payroll Proration Override report. 
 Note: Workday doesn't enable tenant override for the Work Schedule Calendar Change category. 
The Assign Work Schedule event is enabled for smart payroll calculation and retro payroll processing. 
 When you assign work schedule calendars at the worker level and a change in work schedule calendar triggers proration, Workday applies the Assign Work Schedule event for the affected date range for the worker's primary position only. When you assign work schedule calendars by position, Workday applies the proration event for the date range for the position on which the change occurred. 
 When the date of the work schedule calendar change event, including new assignments, is after your opt-in date for assigning work schedule calendars by position, retro payroll processes the change. When your opt-in date is after the event date, retro doesn't pick up the work schedule calendar change. 
 Note: If you select Work Schedule Calendar Change as an event causing pay component proration but don't select the Enable Work Schedule Calendar Assignment by Position, when a work schedule calendar assignment changes, Workday creates proration subperiods based on work shift data.

title: Cancel Pay Complete Performance Update
desc: We make foundational processing updates to Payroll that may help performance.

title: Corrective Accounting for Retroactive Pay and Reallocation Status Management
desc:
Workday updates retroactive payroll processing to support corrective pay accounting, ensuring that journal lines accurately reverse original source period parameters exactly as they were originally created. 
 To prevent ledger discrepancies, Workday also expands the transaction tracking framework of the Payroll Accounting Reallocation (PAR) process by introducing two new operational transaction statuses: On Hold and Requires Recalculation. Workday automatically handles transitions between these statuses throughout the payroll calculation, completion, and cancellation cycles to prevent concurrency conflicts and maintain alignment across your general ledger tables.
benefits: This feature improves financial data integrity by ensuring that retroactive reversals mirror historical accounting lines rather than tracking against current target period configurations. Automated status management eliminates data corruption risks caused by running concurrent allocation and payroll processing jobs over the same populations. User interface guardrails optimize page loading performance, offer clearer operational warnings, and provide multi-select batch flexibility to reduce manual filtering effort for payroll administrators.
changes:
With this update, reversing journal lines for earnings, employer deductions, and employee deductions now reverse historical calculations based on configuration details from their original source periods. 
 All key journal line components, including budget dates, costing companies, credits and debits, hours, ledger accounts, and worktags, now follow source-period values and ignore the current target period's retroactive costing rules. 
 We also update Workday's behavior when you run pay accounting reallocation on retroactive pay results. Workday now excludes retro reversal and retro source payroll result lines from PAR processing and filters out lines that cancel each other out between source and target periods. When you have Salary Over the Cap enabled, Workday now applies the same exclusions during salary over the cap calculations for PAR. 
 To protect data integrity, Workday now automatically bypasses corrective retroactive logic and falls back to standard target period configurations if a currency rate change occurs during the period, or if the underlying source payroll result line has Payroll Accounting Adjustment lines attached. 
 User Interface and Task Enhancements 
 With this release, we deliver several visual and operational updates across pay accounting reallocation tasks: 
     • To improve tenant performance and prevent accidental mass actions, the Workers to Be Processed grid on both the Run Payroll Accounting Reallocation and Cancel Payroll Accounting Reallocation tasks now initializes as empty by default. The grid will only display worker lines when you specify a value on the Worker or Status fields. 
    • We introduce validation to the Cancel Payroll Accounting Reallocation task. If you leave both the Worker and Status fields empty and attempt to select the Ok to Proceed check box, the task is blocked, and the system displays an error message. 
    • We enhance validation logic on the Maintain Payroll Accounting Options task. On the Accounting Reallocation tab, the system now prevents you from disabling core reallocation check boxes if transactions in your tenant exist in Error, In Progress, On Hold, or Requires Recalculation statuses. 
    • We add informational hover text tooltips to prompt fields on the Run and Cancel tasks to guide data entry. 
    • We update the Important Notes displayed on the Run and Complete tasks to explicitly account for the expanded concurrency rules and status options. 
 Object and Operational Rule Changes 
 We update the Pay Accounting Reallocation by Status Report to enable you to select and display the new On Hold and Requires Recalculation statuses. 
 Workday adds sequential execution rules for reallocation job types. If an active task is running, incoming reallocation or status update jobs will automatically be held in a queued state if they share overlapping workers, pay group details, or pay periods

title: Dependent Effective Dating
desc: With this release, Workday adds effective-dated logic to certain dependent data.
benefits: Effective-dated dependent data ensures accurate eligibility tracking, regulatory compliance, and reliable reporting over time.
changes:
Label Name Updates on the View Dependent Task 
 We add the new label View Dependent As Of at the top of the View Dependent task page. This new label displays the effective date of the dependent data you're viewing. In the same task, we rename the label Effective Date to Relationship Effective From. This label indicates the date the relationship status went into effect. This update is automatically available in Preview tenants as of 2026-08-07. 
 Effective Date Correction 
 With this update, we enable workers to edit the effective date of when they added or edited a dependent if the date they initially selected is incorrect. This update helps to eliminate the need to cancel the entire dependent event and start a new one just to correct the effective date. 
 Note: Effective date correction is only allowed before event submission. 
 If your dependent event business process includes a review (such as Verify Dependent Eligibility) or approval step before the completion step, a benefits administrator or partner can send the event back to the worker if the effective date needs to be corrected. The worker can then correct the effective date on the Revise Dependent Event task, and resubmit the dependent for review and approval. 
 UI Changes 
 We add the new Effective Date prompt as an initiating element when you access these tasks: 
 Add Dependent 
 Add My Dependent 
 Edit Dependent 
 Edit My Dependent 
 View Dependent 
 The Effective Date prompt assigns an effective date to these areas of dependent information: 
 Allowed for tax deduction 
 Annual Income 
 Contact Information - Address (1 primary address and up to 2 additional addresses) 
 Disabled 
 Full-time student 
 Health care coverage available elsewhere 
 Legal Name 
 Lives with worker 
 Occupation 
 Relationship 
 Tobacco Use 
 We remove the individual effective dates for these fields, as they now inherit the effective date you enter when initiating the updated tasks: 
     • Allowed for tax deduction 
    • Annual Income 
    • Health care coverage available elsewhere 
    • Lives with Worker 
    • Occupation 
 Next, if you edit a dependent’s information, and that dependent is also listed as your beneficiary or emergency contact, that dependent’s updated information will now also be applied to those areas. When a dependent is added or updated as a beneficiary, Workday creates 2 separate event records with different effective dates: 
     • Dependent event: Uses the effective date specified on the event. 
    • Beneficiary event: Uses today's date as the effective date. 
 You can also now add dependents as of any specified effective date. For dependents effective in the future, we add the new Future Dependents grid to the My Dependents tab of the Benefits page in a worker’s profile. Note that existing dependents are effective as of the effective date specified in the original dependent creation event. You can view this date in worker history. 
 We add the new column Actions to the new Future Dependents grid and the existing Current Dependents grid. This column contains the new Actions dropdown menu with these options: 
 Edit 
    • View 
    • Delete (available only for dependents not enrolled in benefit elections) 
 The View option now enables you to view dependent information as of a specified effective date 
 Note: Future-dated dependents created outside enrollment events can't be added to events where they're not yet effective. Example: an event with an event date prior to the dependents' future effective date. 
 Dependents created outside enrollment can be included in events and enrolled in benefit plans, provided they're effective and eligible as of the plan's coverage begin date. 
 By default, dependents added during enrollment events become effective on the earliest date of these dates: 
     • The dependent's creation date. 
    • The event date. 
    • The plan's coverage begin date. 
 You can't choose a specific effective date for dependents created during enrollment. 
 Reporting 
 We deliver these new report fields on the Dependent business object to represent dependent data as of an effective date (secured to the Worker Data: Dependents domain): 
 Dependent Relationship Type - Effective Dated 
 Legal Name - Effective Dated 
 Related Person Relationship Behavior - Effective Dated 
 We also deliver these new report fields on the Dependent business object (secured to Public Reporting Items): 
 Legal Name - First Name (Effective Dated) 
 Legal Name - Last Name (Effective Dated) 
 Legal Name - Middle Name (Effective Dated) 
 Legal Name - Salutation (Effective Dated) 
 Legal Name - Social Suffix (Effective Dated) 
 Legal Name - Title (Effective Dated) 
 We also update existing report fields to now represent dependent data as of an effective date. We list both the new report fields and the updated, existing report fields in the spreadsheet New and Updated Effective-Dated Dependent Report Fields attached to this release note. 
 Finally, we update the existing Dependents Audit report to use the effective-dated report fields. 
 Web Services 
 We update these web services to require an effective date: 
 Add Dependent 
 Edit Dependent 
 Get Add Dependent 
 These web service updates are available in Preview tenants with v44.2 as of 2025-05-30. These web service updates will deliver to Production tenants with v47 on the target date of 2026-09-19.

desc:
With this release, we deliver Enhanced Direct Deposit (EDD). EDD enables workers to create or select an existing U.S. bank account from external financial partners through employee self-service payment elections. 
 Payroll for the U.S. customers can use EDD to: 
     • Enable and authenticate external financial partners for their workers. 
    • Retrieve and apply banking details to workers’ payment elections.
benefits:
EDD enables your workers to select a financial partner and create an account with them. When workers choose to create an account with a partner, Workday automatically updates the workers’ direct deposit payment elections to their new account. If a worker has an existing account with a financial partner, they can choose that partner and Workday will update their direct deposit payment elections as well. This functionality helps save time and reduce errors caused by manual entry of account data. 
 You can enable or disable the EDD financial partners that your workers can access.

The Enhanced Direct Deposit tab contains a list of financial partners that are enabled by default for your workers to select to use for their payment elections. You can disable the financial partners that you don’t want to make available to your workers.

 The new page displays a Connect Instantly section featuring the enabled financial partners. Selecting a financial partner launches a consent notice informing the worker that they are leaving Workday to authenticate with the partner. 
 After completing partner authentication, workers are redirected back to Workday payment elections with a message confirming that Workday has updated their payment elections with their partner account. 
 Partner bank accounts require USD as the currency prompt selection on desktop, mobile, and administrative updates.

title: Exclude Workers from Retro Pay Calculation
desc: We deliver a new prompt on the Run Retro Pay Calculation task that enables you to exclude specific workers from a retro run who cause processing delays or job failures for a retro pay calculation.
benefits: This prevents individual worker errors from delaying retroactive payroll, so that you can calculate the remaining pay group and period successfully.
changes:
When you select specific Pay Groups or Pay Group Details along with an ~Employees~ to Calculate option, you can now exclude workers from those pay groups using the ~Employees~ to Exclude prompt under the Exclude ~Employees~ section on the Run Retro Pay Calculation task. When excluding a worker in Run Retro Pay Calculation, it's only for that run. The worker will be processed again in any subsequent Run Retro Pay Calculation unless they are excluded again. 
 
 
 
 On the View Background Process page, we display ~Workers~ Excluded from Processing under the Calculation Criteria tab. 
 
 We also update the Retro Pay Calculation Results Volume Report to display the ~Workers~ Excluded from Processing column. 
 
 Behavior Differences for Active and Terminated Workers: 
     • If you exclude an active worker from a Retro Pay Calculation run and then Run Retro Pay Complete, in the next Retro Pay Calculation run, the active worker that was previously excluded will be processed again. 
    • If you exclude a terminated worker from a Retro Pay Calculation run and then Run Retro Pay Complete, in the next Retro Pay Calculation run, the terminated worker that was previously excluded will no longer be processed unless there is a new retro event entered or you select the option to run retro, specifically, for the terminated worker. 
    • If an In Progress retro result for a worker should be excluded from a subsequent retro run, the retro result needs to be cancelled before the next Run Retro Pay Calculation run is initiated. Once the retro result is cancelled, you can initiate another Run Retro Pay Calculation run indicating the worker should be excluded in the Exclude Employees section.

title: U.S. Federal - Personnel Action Request Payroll Status Indicator

changes:
Personnel Action Status 
 The Personnel Action Status field enables you to convey the Payroll Integration status of a single Personnel Action Request (PAR). You can edit the Personnel Action Status field when you access Business Process > Correct from the related actions menu on a Personnel Action Request business process event, or by using the Import Personnel Action Status Update web service. The EHRI integration submits the PAR event.

    • An error message displays under the Messages section - This pay component has a circular reference calculation that you need to review and fix or the payroll result amounts may be incorrect. 
    • The impacted pay component displays in the Business Object column 
    • The impacted period and pay group detail display in the Target(s) column. 
 
    • On each impacted payroll result:     • The individual payroll results with circular calculations are in Error status. 
    • The Calculation Error(s) tab appears with the affected pay component in the Calculation column with the error message - Pay result has a circular calculation which could not be calculated, and the result amounts may be incorrect. 
 
 When you select the check box, and a circular calculation is detected: 
     • On the background process page:     • The job status is complete with warnings. 
    • A warning message displays in the Messages section on the job background process page - This pay component has a circular reference calculation that you need to review and fix or the payroll result amounts may be incorrect. 
    • The impacted pay component displays in the Business Object column, and the impacted period, pay group detail displays in the Target(s) column. 
 
 If you change the Limit to Job Warning for Circular Calculation setting while a calculation job is running, the job maintains its original starting behavior. For example, if you enable the check box while a job is executing, the individual results will still error out if you’ve disabled the configuration at kickoff. 
 Note: This feature enables you to bypass hard stops and complete your payroll processing in a tight timeframe, when circular calculation issues are detected. 
 Workday recommends against leaving this feature enabled for extended periods. It should only be used as a temporary workaround to complete an urgent payroll cycle. If you enable this feature, you must manually validate the affected results, make any necessary manual adjustments before finalization, and resolve the underlying circular reference as soon as the payroll window closes.

title: Compensation Step Adjustment Mass Operation Management
desc: With this release, Workday introduces a new Mass Operation Management task type to update compensation step defaults and generate compensation events for eligible workers at scale. Administrators can now apply percentage-based or amount-based increases to target populations based on a top-down selection hierarchy of packages, grades, and profiles.
benefits: This enhancement streamlines mass compensation adjustments, reducing manual effort and processing time for administrators. It also improves accuracy and helps to ensure compliance for U.S. federal agencies by automatically generating associated Personnel Action Request events alongside the compensation events.
changes:
Security 
 We add the new Compensation Step Adjustment option to the Access to Segments field in the Access Rights section of the Create Security Group task when you create a segment-based security group. 
 UI Changes 
 We deliver the new Compensation Step Adjustment option to the Mass Operation Type field of the Mass Operation Management task. This new mass operation type enables compensation administrators to initiate bulk amount-based or percent-based updates to compensation step defaults. 
 When you run this mass operation type, Workday first evaluates the compensation steps you want to adjust. If valid, Workday then evaluates the positions that are assigned those steps. If the positions are valid, Workday creates and completes step adjustment compensation events for all workers on those positions. If a step or position is invalid, Workday bypasses it in the mass compensation adjustment. 
 Workday bypasses compensation steps that are: 
     • Undergoing an in-progress individual or mass adjustment event. 
    • Inactive. 
    • (Amount-based adjustments only) Configured with a Currency or Frequency that doesn't match the Currency or Frequency you select for the mass operation. 
 Workday bypasses positions that are: 
     • Undergoing an in-progress compensation review. 
    • Undergoing an in-progress compensation event, including hold events such as Leave of Absence. 
    • Configured with the Do Not Adjust allowed action in either the Employees Using Default section or the Employees Using Override section in the mass operation configuration. 
    • (U.S. federal) Assigned a pay and/or grade retention status using Pay Rate Determinants of the Grade Retention or Pay Retention type. 
 You can select the Validate Only button to preview the validation of steps and positions without committing data or creating actual compensation events. 
 Note that the lowest level of Report Definition selection receives the mass compensation step adjustment. See the Example section under the Testing tab of this release note for more information. 
 (U.S. federal) In the Personnel Action Request Setup task, we add the new Compensation Step Adjustment option in the Mass Action section. When U.S. federal users select this option, Workday reveals new PAR fields in the mass operation task. When you run the mass action, Workday initiates and completes a Personnel Action Request event for each worker who receives a compensation event as a result of the mass action. The data you add to the PAR fields apply to all PARs created from this mass action. 
 Reporting 
 We deliver the new Active Compensation Steps report (secured to the Set Up: Compensation Steps domain in the Core Compensation functional area). This report uses the new Active Compensation Steps report data source. You can copy this report to use as your own custom report for the mass operation’s required Input Report.

title: Prompt Updates for AI-Generated Development Items
desc: We now update the Generate with AI prompt for development items in the Career Hub and Manager Insights Hub, enabling workers and managers to view AI-generated descriptions before adding them to development items.
benefits:
We make the interface for AI-generated development items more consistent with other Generate with AI prompts in Workday. 
 We make it easier for workers and managers to leverage AI-generated content, on its own or combined with their own writing.
changes:
We replace the Generate with AI and Modify with AI buttons with a standardized Generate with AI prompt. We surface this prompt as an AI edit icon in the Additional Details field. Workers can access Generate with AI and Modify with AI options from this prompt. 
 
 When workers or managers use the Generate with AI, Make More Challenging, or Make Easier options while creating a development item in the Career Hub or Manager Insights Hub, we now:

title: Minimum Wage Analysis Skill for the Payroll Agent
desc: With this release, we continue to deliver updates to the Minimum Wage Analysis Skill for the Payroll Agent by adding support for U.S. local authorities.

 See:
