title: No Pay Accounting Reallocation Prior To Date
desc:
With this release, we update the Maintain Payroll Accounting Options task to introduce the No Pay Accounting Reallocation Prior To date, which enables you to prevent pay accounting reallocations from processing pay periods that end before the specified date. 
 We also add a Pay Accounting Reallocation Status field on Assign Costing Allocation events and reports so you can identify reallocation eligibility and processing outcomes, including periods excluded by the prior-to date.
benefits:
The No Pay Accounting Reallocation Prior To date helps protect sensitive, audited, or reconciled pay periods from unintended reallocations. Administrators gain clearer control over how far back they can reallocate payroll accounting without recalculating pay results. 
 Visibility into the reallocation status of costing allocations improves auditability. You can identify which costing allocations are eligible, in progress, complete, or excluded because they fall before your configured date.
changes:
We add an optional No Pay Accounting Reallocation Prior To date field on the Accounting Reallocation tab of the Maintain Payroll Accounting Options task. 
 When you enter a No Pay Accounting Reallocation Prior To date, Workday evaluates the pay period end date during pay accounting reallocation processing. Depending on the date you specify: 
 Workday does not process reallocations for pay periods with period end dates before the specified date. 
 Workday processes reallocations for pay periods with period end dates on or after the specified date. 
 If you don’t specify a No Pay Accounting Reallocation Prior To date, Workday applies no restriction on processing reallocations. 
 When you attempt to save a new or updated No Pay Accounting Reallocation Prior To date on Maintain Payroll Accounting Options, Workday checks for pay accounting reallocations in Error, In Progress, On Hold, or Requires Recalculation statuses. If any exist, Workday prevents you from saving the date. 
 We also update the Accounting Reallocation tab on the Maintain Payroll Accounting Options task to reorganize configuration settings into these categories: 
 Costing Reallocations 
 Fringe Reallocations 
 Salary Over the Cap Reallocations 
 Reporting 
 We deliver a new Pay Accounting Reallocation Status report field on the Assign Costing Allocation business object (secured to the Public Reporting Items domain). You can add this field to standard and custom reports that include the Assign Costing Allocation business object to display the reallocation status of a costing allocation event.

title: On-Demand Payroll Result Recalculation
desc: Workday improves the process for recalculating an on-demand payroll result, making it faster and more reliable by introducing logic to prevent processing conflicts with other ongoing payroll jobs. Now, when you initiate a recalculation, Workday checks for conflicting processes and queues the job appropriately.
benefits: This improves recalculation time for on-demand payroll results while ensuring that payroll administrators always view the most current and active payroll result.
changes:
Workday now prevents you from recalculating an on-demand payroll result when that result is already being processed by another job. Workday sets the recalculation status to Skipped and redirects you to the on-demand result with instructions on how to proceed. As a result, you might notice faster run times for on-demand payroll result recalculations. 
 You might experience longer run times for complex or large recalculations, such as calculations that include retro or a large volume of pay inputs. Workday displays a pop-up message to let you know that your request is being processed with the option to be notified when it’s complete. Clicking Notify Me Later enables you to continue working in your tenant while Workday processes your recalculation in the background.

title: Percent-Based Bonus Plan Enhancements
desc:
With this release, we enhance percent-based bonus plan functionality by enabling you to use decimal point values to the ten thousandth for Target % fields. 
 Example: You can now enter a value of 5.6599% for the Target % field when creating or editing a percent-based bonus plan.
benefits: This enhancement gives you more granular control and precision over numeric values when determining percent-based bonus plans.
changes:
You can now enter decimal point values to the ten thousandth for Target % when creating or editing percent-based bonus plans and bonus plan profiles. 
 Bonus percent values with decimal point values to the ten thousandth now display on bonus plans, Request Compensation Change events, and Compensation Review events. 
 We deliver these new report fields on the Compensation Review Bonus Payment business object that you can use in custom reports to display decimal point values to the ten thousandth: 
     • Actual Bonus Percent 
    • Target Bonus Percent 
 We update the Put Compensation Plans and Get Compensation Plans web service operations to support bonus percent decimal point values to the ten thousandth.

title: U.S. Federal: Mass Cancel and Mass Correct for Personnel Action Requests
desc: With this release, Workday enables U.S. Federal customers to cancel and correct large volumes of Personnel Action Request events at once from the Find Personnel Action Requests report.
benefits: This feature increases administrator efficiency for federal agencies by reducing time spent on manually cancelling and correcting individual Personnel Action Request events.
changes:
Workday delivers these new initiating actions on the Personnel Action Request business process security policy: 
     • Mass Cancel Personnel Action Request 
    • Mass Correct Personnel Action Request 
 We deliver the new Recently Corrected report field on the Personnel Action business object (secured to the Worker Data: Personnel Action Requests domain). 
 Workday enhances the Find Personnel Action Requests report (secured to the Worker Data: Personnel Action Requests domain) by adding a new Recently Corrected search facet. You can use this search facet to identify completed data corrections that were initiated on parent business processes, and then mass correct those events. This search facet only displays when there are corrected events from the last 30 days. 
 We also add these buttons, enabling users to initiate mass corrections or cancellations (secured to the Mass Action Events domain): 
     • Cancel 
    • Correct 
 Workday automatically approves mass corrections and cancellations, and skips your configured business process reviews and approvals. 
 When a user initiates a mass cancellation or correction from the report, a new modal displays, enabling them to enter Personnel Action Request values. Workday default populates any required values. Once submitted, Workday sends the processing user a task where they can review a table that displays all eligible, selected events. In the table, they can edit Nature of Action, Legal Authority, and Remarks values before they submit. They can edit using one of these methods: 
     • Bulk edit: Select multiple events and click the Mass Edit button. This method enables the user to apply the same values to all selected rows. 
    • Individual edit: Click the Edit button on an individual event to modify the values for that event. 
 Once the user completes edits, they must click Submit Table to submit the mass cancellation or mass correction. 
 To initiate a mass cancellation, the events must be rescindable. Once cancelled, Workday automatically rescinds the parent business process events and creates 001 - Cancellation Personnel Action Request events. 
 For mass corrections, Workday automatically creates 002 - Correction Personnel Action Request events. 
 On the Personnel Action Request tab on the View Worker History by Category task on the worker profile, we add these columns: 
     • Effective Date 
    • Initiated On 
    • Personnel Action Status 
    • Sequence Number 
    • Status 
 
 The new columns are secured to these domains: 
     • Self-Service: Historical Staffing Information 
    • Worker Data: Historical Staffing Information 
 We deliver these new web service operations (secured to the Personnel Action Interface domain) in v46.0 to support cancelling and correcting Personnel Action Request events: 
     • Cancel Personnel Action Request Event 
    • Correct Personnel Action Request Event 
 See the SOAP API Change Log link under Related Information.

title: U.S. Federal: Post-Separation Personnel Action Request Data
desc: With this release, Workday now populates values on personnel action requests and SF-50’s and SF-52’s when U.S. Federal customers process a one-time payment after a worker’s termination. Workday populates values based on the worker's last-held position on their termination date.
benefits: This enhancement ensures that U.S. Federal customers maintain compliant, complete, and audit-ready records for personnel actions.
changes:
Workday enhances the Request One-Time Payment business process. Now, when you initiate a one-time payment after the worker has separated from your organization, Workday populates SF-50 and SF-52 fields with values from the worker’s last held position, in accordance with your configured Nature of Action (NOA) codes. These values also persist on the personnel action request event after separation and display on the printed SF-50 and SF-52. 
 Now, when you process a rehire event with a future effective date, Workday preserves data from previously processed post-separation one-time payments.

title: Worker Addresses Purgeable Data Type
desc: Workday delivers the new Worker Addresses Purgeable Data Type (PDT) that enables you to permanently remove home and work addresses for active workers and terminated workers.
benefits: The new PDT increases your control over your data and supports data protection and global data compliance requirements, including General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) requirements. The PDT includes Workday-delivered validations to block or warn against a data purge that will be impactful to a dependent process such a worker pay or benefits.
changes:
With this update, we deliver the Worker Addresses PDT that you can use to purge all of a worker's home addresses and work addresses. 
     • Home addresses include any current, past, or future primary home address, and any additional home addresses. 
    • Work addresses include any current, past, or future primary work address, and any additional work addresses. 
 This PDT can only be used for purging workers (employee and contingent) addresses. 
 Home addresses that are shared with related persons (Beneficiaries, Dependents, or Emergency Contacts) are unlinked from the worker. Though the worker is no longer using the addresses, the other related persons do. To purge a Beneficiaries address, you must purge the Beneficiary using the Worker’s Beneficiaries (Person and Trust) PDT. 
 If the address is the only or last piece of information purged from a Contact Information event, the Contact Information event will also be purged. If not, the Contact Information event remains because an email, instant messenger, phone, or web address could have been updated in the same event. 
 We also deliver new Worker Addresses PDT blocking validations that cannot be bypassed. They block the purge of an address to prevent system or business disruption. These validation impact addresses used in: 
     • Benefits 
    • Compensation 
    • Expenses 
    • Payroll 
    • Student 
 We also deliver optional validations that reinforce Payroll data retention time periods. These validation are warnings, and can be bypassed. 
 
 See the PDF in the Related Information section for a complete list of these validations. 
 Note: Purging is permanent and irreversible. You can't recover the purged data. We recommend that you test purging in a Sandbox environment first.

title: Pay Accounting Reallocation
desc: Workday introduces pay accounting reallocation, which enables you to process accounting for a prior payroll period based on retroactive costing allocations that could cause updates to accounting when re-processed.
benefits: Pay accounting reallocation will make it easier to process multiple payroll accounting adjustments in order to correct accounting on completed payroll results.
changes:
Run Pay Accounting Reallocation 
 We create the Run Pay Accounting Reallocation task, secured to the Process: Run Payroll Accounting Reallocation domain in the Core Payroll functional area. This task identifies completed costing allocation events and processes them for pay accounting reallocation. It also can reallocate based on retro pay transactions for salary over the cap. 
 You can enter a date in the Completed Through field to select events completed within that date range. You can also run pay accounting reallocation for specific workers. If you don't select any workers, Workday runs reallocations for all workers. 
 Pay accounting reallocation supports: 
 Primary worktag balancing 
 Optional worktag balancing 
 Payroll intercompany accounting 
 Financial intercompany settlement 
 If you run pay accounting reallocation with intercompany accounting enabled and then attempt to disable intercompany accounting, a validation message displays. 
 When the run pay accounting reallocation task is complete, the processed reallocations display, along with the number of workers you selected (if any). The Results grid displays the reallocation transaction status, which corresponds to the journal status. 
 Note: You can’t rescind a costing allocation event if it was used in a reallocation result. If you want to rescind the event, you must first cancel all in-progress reallocation results. 
 When you run pay accounting reallocation, Workday won’t process payroll results with existing payroll accounting adjustments. However, if you rescind the payroll accounting adjustment, you can successfully process that payroll result for reallocation. 
 In addition, you can run a payroll accounting reallocation on top of another payroll accounting reallocation for the same payroll result. For example: you generate a subsequent payroll accounting reallocation for the same payroll result(s) from a costing allocation event at the same costing hierarchy level. 
 If you try to run payroll accounting reallocation while these tasks are in-progress with overlapping workers, a warning message displays and the overlapping workers will not be included in the run: 
 Another Run Pay Accounting Reallocation job 
 Complete Payroll Accounting Reallocation 
 Cancel Payroll Accounting Reallocation 
 Reallocation respects these configurations: 
 Employer Paid Default Costing 
 Grant Begin and Grant End Dates 
 Salary Over the Cap 
 Complete Pay Accounting Reallocation 
 We create a new task, Complete Pay Accounting Reallocation, secured to the Process: Run Payroll Accounting Reallocation domain in the Core Payroll functional area. This enables you to complete all in-progress pay accounting reallocation results for specified workers. If you don't select any workers, reallocations are completed for all workers. 
 The task will also display journal summarization (if enabled), and move any reallocation journals from created to posted status. When you generate reallocation journals and then run the task, the payroll results will not be picked up by any subsequent reallocation jobs. 
 Once the Complete Pay Accounting Reallocation task is finished, the Results grid displays all or selected workers with in progress and in error reallocation results. The numbers in the In Progress or In Error columns are drillable and display: 
 Costing Allocation Event 
 Payroll Result 
 Current Accounting 
 Note: The Complete Pay Accounting Reallocation task can't be reversed or rescinded. 
 You can run Complete Pay Accounting Reallocation while another Run Pay Accounting Reallocation job or Cancel Accounting Reallocation job with overlapping workers are in progress. However, a warning message displays and the overlapping workers are excluded if you run Complete Pay Accounting Reallocation while these jobs are in-progress: 
 Another Complete Payroll Accounting Reallocation job 
 Run Payroll Accounting Reallocation 
 Cancel Payroll Accounting Reallocation 
 The Reallocation Complete field in the Details tab of a costing allocation event indicates whether payroll account reallocation has been successfully completed for that event. 
 Cancel Pay Accounting Reallocation 
 We create the Cancel Pay Accounting Reallocation task, secured to the Process: Run Payroll Accounting Reallocation domain in the Core Payroll functional area. This task cancels all in progress and in error pay accounting reallocations for workers that you specify. If you don't select any workers, reallocations for all workers are canceled. 
 Once you complete the task, a Results grid displays. If you don’t specify workers, then the grid displays all workers with in progress and in error reallocation results. If you do specify workers, then the grid displays this data for the specified worker(s). The numbers in the In Progress or In Error columns are drillable and display: 
 Costing Allocation Event 
 Payroll Result 
 Current Accounting 
 When the task is complete, the number of selected workers displays, along with pay results with canceled reallocations. 
 If you try to use Cancel Pay Accounting Reallocation while these jobs are in-progress with overlapping workers, a warning message displays and the overlapping workers will not be included in the run: 
 Another Cancel Payroll Accounting Reallocation job 
 Run Payroll Accounting Allocation 
 Complete Payroll Accounting Reallocation 
 Note: You can’t run Cancel Pay Complete for a pay group detail with a worker that has an in progress, in error, or completed reallocation result. 
 If you have not enabled journal summarization but you want to apply it to in-progress payroll, you must first use Cancel Pay Accounting Reallocation to erase all existing journals and then use Run Pay Accounting Reallocation to recreate the journals. You can’t disable journal summarization once a summary journal is created. 
 Reallocation for Retro Results 
 Workday supports reallocation for salary over the cap inclusive of retro pay results. 
 A payroll result requires pay accounting reallocation if you meet these criteria: 
 You run gross-to-net retro. 
 Workday generates at least one retro journal line with a salary over the cap grant. 
 You run Pay Complete or complete payroll through mass actions or related actions. 
 If you use gross-to-net retro processing with a salary over the cap grant and then you run pay accounting reallocation: 
 Workday recalculates salary over the cap for the result via the reallocation journal, considering all wages for the period (inclusive of retro differences for earnings in the salary over the cap pay component group). 
 Workday includes the result in subsequent Run Pay Accounting Reallocation jobs. 
 We create the Enable Reallocation of Retro Results for Salary Over the Cap setting in the Maintain Payroll Accounting Options task. This ensures you can run reallocation jobs and process gross-to-net retro results for salary over the cap. 
 Once enabled, you can only disable the setting if there are no reallocation results in progress or in error. If disabled, Workday won’t process any results that require reallocation due to gross-to-net retro differences. 
 You can’t select the Enable Reallocation of Retro Results for Salary Over the Cap setting unless you first select these settings in the Maintain Payroll Accounting Options task: 
 Enable Payroll Accounting Reallocation 
 Salary Over the Cap – Enable 
 Enable Retro Costing 
 Note: If a retro difference causes the total institutional base salary to decrease lower than the cap amount for a source period, then everything is costed under the cap. 
 We create the No Retro Reallocation Prior To setting in the Maintain Payroll Accounting Options task. When enabled, Workday won’t process any gross-to-net retro reallocations for payroll results with a period end date prior to the date you configure. 
 We create the Maximum Months Allowed For Retro Reallocation setting in the Maintain Payroll Accounting Options task. This allows you to define a maximum number of months that Workday will look back to for gross-to-net retro for reallocation processing. This works in conjunction with the No Retro Pay Reallocation Prior To Date setting to provide more accounting flexibility. 
 Reporting 
 Workday creates the Excluded Pay Results from Pay Accounting Reallocation report. This report displays payroll results excluded from a Run Pay Accounting Reallocation job due to an existing payroll accounting adjustment for that payroll result. You can use this report to identify pay results that were not reallocated that might need additional adjustment. 
 We also update these reports: 
     • Process Monitor report- Now displays details about reallocation. 
    • View Payroll Result report- Now displays Payroll Account Reallocation journals on the Other Accounting tab. 
 We update these reports to include Payroll Accrual Reallocation as a journal source: 
 Payroll Accounting By Company/Period 
 Payroll Accounting By Period/Pay Group 
 This enables you to find journal lines associated with pay accounting reallocations. 
 We add a new Exclude Reversal Journal Lines check box to these reports that enables you to generate reports without reversal journal line results. 
 We deliver these new report fields that you can use in custom reports: 
 Payroll Reversed Journal Line 
 Payroll Reversing Journal Line 
 Journal Source for Excluding Reversing Journal Lines 
 Payroll Results 
 If a pay result has either an in progress or completed payroll accounting reallocation, you can’t reverse that pay result. However, if you cancel an in progress result, then you can still reverse it, assuming that the result has not yet been reconciled. Once the accounting for a result is reconciled, the result cannot be reversed. 
 Web Services 
 We update the Put Journal Source Mappings to Operational Transactions and Get Journal Source Mappings to Operational Transactions web services with these new fields: 
 Payroll Accrual Reallocation Journal Entry Source Reference 
 Fringe Benefit Reallocation Journal Entry Source Reference 
 Note: The Fringe Benefit Reallocation Journal Entry Source Reference field is viewable, but will not generate results in Workday. Fringe Benefit Reallocation will be available at a future date. 
 You can use the Put Account Posting Rule Set web service to enter the Payroll Accrual Reallocation journal source in the Account Posting Rule Condition Value Reference field. You can use the Get Account Posting Rule Set web service to retrieve the field as well. 
 Accounting Journals 
 We add these new payroll journal sources: 
 Payroll Accrual Reallocation 
 Fringe Benefit Reallocation 
 Note: The Fringe Benefit Reallocation journal source is viewable, but is not actionable in Workday. Reallocation for fringe benefit accounting will be available at a future date. 
 You can access these journal sources in the Values drop-down in the Dimension column in the Edit Account Posting Rules task. With this task, you can add the journal sources to these account posting rules: 
 Payroll Deduction 
 Payroll Earnings 
 Payroll Expense 
 Fringe Benefit Expense 
 Fringe Benefit Recovery 
 The Payroll Journal Source dimension is respected when evaluating APRs to determine ledger account for the reallocation lines. 
 When you access the Maintain Journal Source Mapping to Operational Transactions task, you can now apply the Payroll Actual Accrual Reallocation journal entry source. 
 When you access the View Journal Source Mapping to Operational Transactions report, the Payroll Actual Accrual Reallocation journal entry source displays with Payroll Accrual Reallocation journal source. 
 We add a new In Use column to the Maintain Journal Sources task. If In Use is selected in the Payroll Accrual Reallocation row, it indicates that the Payroll Accrual Reallocation is mapped to the Payroll Actual Accrual journal entry source in the Maintain Journal Source Mapping to Operational Transactions task. 
 If you remove this mapping in the Maintain Journal Source Mapping to Operational Transactions task, the In Use column will be blank. 
 Note: Costing allocation changes for a completed period should be completed before you access the Run Pay Accounting Reallocation task.

title: Compensation Plan Rollout Process
desc: With this release, we deliver a new report, report data source, and report fields that enable you to access results for the compensation rollout process.
benefits: This feature enables you to access compensation rollout process results more quickly and efficiently, while using less tenant resources. The updates to the View Compensation Plan Rollout Process task also provide an enhanced user experience when reviewing rollout process details.
changes:
We deliver: 
     • A new Compensation Plan Rollout Process Results report (secured to the Process: Plan Adjustments Reporting and Web Services domain) that is accessible from the View Compensation Plan Rollout Process task. 
    • A new Eligible Positions for Compensation Plan Rollout Process report data source (secured to the Process: Plan Adjustments Reporting and Web Services domain). You can use the report data source to create custom reports for positions eligible for a compensation rollout process as of the Effective Date. 
 Note: The Compensation Plan Rollout Process Results report is not searchable. You can only access it from the View Compensation Plan Rollout Process task. 
 We deliver these new report fields on the Position business object (secured to the Process: Plan Adjustments Reporting and Web Services domain) that you can use in custom reports: 
     • Pending Business Process Preventing Assignment of Plan 
    • Plan Already Assigned 
    • Employee Received Plan During Compensation Plan Rollout Process 
 We deliver these new report fields on the Compensation Plan Rollout Process business object (secured to the Process: Plan Adjustments Reporting and Web Services domain) that you can use in custom reports: 
     • Compensation Eligibility Rules for Compensation Plan Rollout Process 
    • Compensation Plans for Compensation Plan Rollout Process

title: Learning Courses Linking to Development Items
desc: With this release, workers can link Learning catalog courses directly to their development items using a dedicated Learning field on Development Items. title: Simultaneous Compensation Changes Using Mass Compensation Actions During In Progress Change Job Event
desc: With this release, Workday adds more simultaneous compensation change capabilities by enabling you to allow mass compensation actions to process workers who have an in-progress Change Job event, regardless of whether or not the Change Job event includes compensation changes.
benefits: This feature helps organizations that need to process pay-changing actions on overlapping effective dates while a Change Job promotion or other staffing action remains in progress.
changes:
UI Changes 
 When you opt in, Workday allows you to run these mass compensation actions for workers with an in-progress Change Job event: 
     • Calculation Plan Assignment Updates by Position (in Mass Operation Management). 
    • Compensation Step Adjustment (in Mass Operation Management). 
    • Schedule Automatic Step Progression. 
    • Set Up Compensation Step Adjustment. 
 (U.S. federal) For PAR-enabled mass actions, Workday applies existing Personnel Action Request sequencing behavior. When the worker has another PAR event on the same effective date, Workday defaults the sequence number to 0 for the subsequent action. A sequence number of 0 means the PAR event will process last. 
 Reporting 
 We deliver the Simultaneous Events During Employee Compensation Event report field on the Employee Compensation Event business object (secured to the Worker Data: Staffing domain in the Staffing functional area). Use this report field in your custom reports to return worker events that were in progress at the time the specified employee compensation event was created.

title: U.S. Federal: Personnel Action Request Sequence Alerts
desc: Workday enhances the personnel action request framework by introducing alerts when there are multiple personnel action request events for a worker with the same effective date.
benefits: This enhancement helps U.S. Federal customers maintain regulatory compliance and data integrity.
changes:
With this update, we prevent U.S. Federal customers from processing personnel action request events for a worker that have both the same effective date and the same sequence number (when the sequence number is something other than zero). Workday now provides alerts in the user interface to notify you when a worker’s personnel action request events have the same effective date, and prompt you to ensure that each event has a unique sequence number or a sequence number of zero. 
 Note: The sequence number denotes the order in which your other systems process personnel action requests. Events with a sequence number of zero are processed at the end, at random.

title: UK Salary Sacrifice for Payroll Third-Party Payments
desc: With this release, Workday adds support for United Kingdom (UK) Salary Sacrifice in Payroll Third-Party Payments. You can configure deduction recipients to process salary sacrifice earnings and send employee contribution amounts to third-party recipients correctly.
benefits: You can support UK salary sacrifice arrangements, such as pension and childcare, through Payroll Third-Party Payments without manual adjustments. Workday processes employee contribution amounts so payments to agencies reflect the correct values.
changes:
Workday adds UK salary sacrifice support to Payroll Third-Party Payments on the deduction recipient. 
 You can now: 
 Select an earning in the Pay Component field for United Kingdom deduction recipients 
 When the deduction recipient country is the United Kingdom and an earning is selected in the Pay Component field, Enable Salary Sacrifice will be automatically selected. The selection of this option is an indicator to the pay calc engine that the sign of the amount on payable items created for employee earning contributions should be flipped. 
    • Process employee salary sacrifice amounts so Workday sends the correct payment amount to the third-party recipient. 
 Workday updates the Put Payroll Deduction Recipient and Get Payroll Deduction Recipient web services to support the new fields.

 This update is part of a phased initiative to enhance Workday's ability to support workers with multiple positions across Absence, Payroll, and Time Tracking.
benefits: These new instance value calculations help you to process payroll accurately for workers with multiple positions or midperiod staffing changes, because the calculations use the days or hours from the work schedule calendar for a specific position.

title: Simultaneous Compensation Changes Using Request Quality Step Increase and Request Compensation Change
desc: With this release, Workday adds more simultaneous compensation change capabilities by enabling you to process simultaneous in-progress Request Quality Step Increase (QSI) and Request Compensation Change (RCC) processes for the same worker.
benefits: This change allows you to process simultaneous compensation changes, simplifying ad-hoc pay adjustments in your workforce and streamlining compliance with policies and regulations.
changes:
Using an opt-in tenant configuration, Workday now allows you to initiate a Request Quality Step Increase process when an in-progress Request Compensation Change process already exists for the same worker. 
 Conversely, Workday also now allows you to initiate a Request Compensation Change process when an in-progress Request Quality Step Increase process already exists for the same worker. You can also configure your tenant to enable a Request Compensation Change process through web services and EIB when an in-progress Quality Step Increase exists for the same worker population. 
 When you opt in, Workday: 
     • Disables the validation that blocks you from initiating a Request Compensation Change process when a Request Quality Step Increase process is already in-progress, or vice versa. The tenant configuration disables validation on these processes for initiating actions only. All subsequent business process steps will honor normal business process policies. You can opt out at any time, and existing in-progress events will complete as normal. 
    • Displays In Progress and Future Dated Events on the Request Quality Step Increase task if the worker has relevant events.

title: Payroll Processing Conflict Restrictions
desc: Workday extends conflicting-job processing restrictions to the Cancel Pay Complete and Payroll On Demand Pay Calculation jobs. When these jobs are in progress for a pay run detail, Workday prevents additional processing on results with the same pay run detail until the job completes.
benefits: This enhancement helps payroll administrators avoid processing conflicts that can delay payroll processing and degrade tenant performance. By blocking concurrent payroll result actions while Cancel Pay Complete or Payroll On Demand Pay Calculation runs, your team can reduce the risk of long-running or high-priority jobs and improve overall payroll processing stability.
changes:
When Cancel Pay Complete or Payroll On Demand Pay Calculation is in progress for a pay run detail, Workday now restricts related actions on payroll results in that same pay run detail. Workday applies this restriction across these payroll result related actions for on-cycle, on-demand, and manual payment results: 
 Accounting 
 Cancel 
 Complete 
 Hold 
 Recalculate 
 Unhold 
 Update Input/Recalculate 
 When you click Complete Results from the Payroll Calculation Processing Report, payroll results from the same pay run detail appear under Results Ineligible for Complete in the Conflicting Job in Progress section and are not completed. 
 Workday also prevents you from reviewing and approving an on demand event for the same pay run detail during Cancel Pay Complete or Payroll On Demand Calculation, and from attempting to rescind a Pay On Demand Request for the same pay run detail.

title: Payroll Third-Party Payments: Salary Sacrifice Enhancements
desc: With this release, Workday enhances Payroll Third-Party Payments and Payroll Accounting for United Kingdom (UK) salary sacrifice arrangements.
benefits:
This update: 
     • Enables you to support United Kingdom (UK) salary sacrifice arrangements, such as pension and childcare, through Payroll Third-Party Payments with correct contribution amounts to third-party providers. 
    • Represents salary sacrifice amounts as liabilities to third-party providers rather than reductions in expense, aligning journals with standard accounting principles. 
    • Reduces the need for manual payment and period-end accounting adjustments and reconciliations.
changes:
We update the Create Deduction Recipient and Edit Deduction Recipient tasks for UK deduction recipients. We deliver: 
     • A new Enable Salary Sacrifice check box in the Payroll Third-Party Payments grid. The check box is available only when the deduction recipient country is the United Kingdom and the Pay Component is an earning. When you select an earning, Workday automatically selects Enable Salary Sacrifice. When you generate payable items for an employee contribution, Workday reverses the sign of the amount. For employer contribution rows where Pay Component is a deduction. 
 
You can now: 
    • Use Deduction Recipient as a dimension on the Account Posting Rules task to route salary sacrifice amounts to specific liability ledger accounts based on the third-party benefit provider. 
 
Workday now: 
    • Processes employee salary sacrifice amounts so payments to third-party recipients reflect the correct values. 
    • Posts negative salary sacrifice earnings as a positive credit when the Salary Sacrifice checkbox is selected. 
    • Relieves the liability on Payroll Third party Payments payment journals and records the credit to cash. 
    • Applies pay-period currency conversion to salary sacrifice lines on the Payroll Actuals Journal and related balancing lines when pay group and ledger currencies differ. 
    • Posts realized gain or loss on payment journals when currency conversion rates differ between the pay group currency and the company ledger currency. 
 When you don’t select the Salary Sacrifice check box when creating or editing deduction recipients, Workday continues to generate a negative debit. 
 Web Services 
 For v47.0, Workday updates the Put Payroll Deduction Recipient and Get Payroll Deduction Recipient web service operations to support the Enable Salary Sacrifice and Pay Component fields. 
 See the SOAP API Change Log link under Related Information. 
 
To use this feature, you must have access to these domains: 
Set Up: Payroll Accounting 
Set Up: Tenant Accounting 
Set Up: Payroll (Payroll Third-Party Payments)

title: Custom Calculated Health Care Rates

title: Report Trailing Payments to Prior Pay Groups with PECI
desc: We update the Payroll Effective Change Interface (PECI) integration template to report one-time payments and other retro-dated changes to a worker's prior pay group after the worker changes pay groups.
benefits: With this update, you can now report trailing one-time payments to the payroll company even if a worker changes pay groups. This eliminates the need for manual tracking and input, as the integration can now report retro changes affecting a prior pay group.
changes:
With this update, we deliver a new Report Changes After Pay Group Removal integration service and related integration attributes on the Payroll Effective Change Interface integration template. When a worker switches pay groups and you make a retro one-time payment to the worker's prior pay group, the integration reports the one-time payment in the prior pay group when you enable the new integration service and configure the new integration attributes. 
 We deliver these new integration attributes on the Payroll Effective Change Interface integration template: 
 Report Changes After Pay Group Removal Number of Years Limit integration attribute. Select a value from 1 through 5 years. The default value is 1 year. 
 Override Compensation One-Time Payment Assignment Date integration attribute. When you set this attribute to Effective Date, the integration uses the effective date of the compensation one-time payment to determine the pay group that it reports in or the pay group that processes it. 
 We also update the Maintain External Payroll Input for Worker task by: 
 Delivering a new Pay Group Lookup Date field. Only use this field to target a retro or current dated payroll input OTP (one-time payment) to a prior pay group. Example: For a worker who switched pay groups on 2026-04-01, set the Pay Group Lookup Date to 2026-03-31 to target a payroll input OTP to their prior pay group (with the integration service enabled). This field doesn’t apply to the Payroll Interface integration.

title: Request Edit Payroll Inputs Business Process
desc: We deliver a new Request Edit Payroll Inputs business process that enables payroll partners to request edits to unprocessed and eligible ongoing payroll inputs. Payroll administrators can review, approve, deny, or send back those requests from My Tasks.
benefits: This feature helps you establish a controlled, approval-based workflow for editing payroll inputs by enabling payroll partners to formally request changes to inputs they can view but don't have direct edit access to. This reduces the risk of unauthorized and unaudited payroll modifications and gives payroll administrators full visibility into proposed changes before they take effect. This separation of duties supports stronger internal controls and a more transparent payroll input management process.
changes:
Workday delivers a new Request Edit Payroll Input related action that you can access from a payroll input. 
 Users need View and Modify access to the Worker Data: Payroll (Payroll Input) domain to initiate and review requests. 
 
 Payroll partners can use this new related action to: 
     • Initiate an edit request for unprocessed one-time payroll inputs when there is no in-progress Edit Payroll Input, Request Edit Payroll Input, or Request Delete Payroll Input event for the same input. 
    • Request changes for the End Date for unprocessed ongoing payroll inputs, or for calculated ongoing payroll inputs with a future or open-ended End Date; all other fields are read-only. You can still add a payroll input attachment. 
    • Update the allowed payroll input values on the request, attach supporting files if needed, then submit or cancel the request for unprocessed one-time inputs. The request form displays all editable fields except Worker, which is read-only, and Special Entry, which is hidden. 
 When a payroll partner submits a request, the payroll administrator receives a Request Edit Payroll Input review task in their My Tasks. The review task displays the current payroll input details alongside the proposed changes, with a comparison showing the field, current details, and proposed changes for each modified value. The administrator can approve, send back, deny, or cancel the request. When the administrator approves the request, Workday applies the edits to the payroll input and marks any uncompleted payroll results associated with that input, including retro results, as Required for recalculation. 
 Workday validates requests and displays messages when these conflicts exist:When the payroll input is modified after the request starts and the payroll partner attempts to submit: “You can't submit this request because the payroll input has been modified. Cancel the request.” 
 When another active payroll input request is already in progress for the same input: “You can't complete this request because another one is already in progress. Cancel this request.” 
 When the payroll input is modified after the review starts and the administrator attempts to approve or send back: “This input has been modified since the request has been started. Please deny this request.”

title: Stock Vesting Schedule Enhancements

Compensation administrators can configure specific cliffs, graded vesting periods, and rounding rules natively within the system.
benefits: This feature addresses the manual overhead associated with equity administration by dynamically calculating vesting exposure directly within Workday. Compensation administrators and HR partners no longer need to rely on external spreadsheets or third-party tools to interpret text-based vesting schedules or answer employee equity questions. This ensures higher data accuracy, improves point-in-time reporting, and gives employees clearer visibility into their earned equity.

    • Period.

This column displays True if the Shares Vested and Shares Unvested columns’ values are dynamically generated based on your configuration of the Stock Vesting Schedule Detail subgrid in the Maintain Stock Vesting Schedules task. The Shares Calculated column displays as False if you manually adjust the values in the Shares Vested and Shares Unvested columns and then select OK. If you access this task again, enter 0 in the Shares Vested and Shares Unvested fields, then click OK, Workday defaults back to the calculated values and displays the Shares Calculated column as True.

We also add the Calculated column that displays True if those values are a result of a calculation configured in the Maintain Stock Vesting Schedules task.
